Proscribe

/proh-SKRYB/ - rhymes with tribe · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Proscribe means to condemn or outlaw.

The style manual proscribes exclamation points outside quoted speech, and the editors enforce it with relish.

Worked Example

After a second stargazer tumbled in the dark, the observatory proscribed white flashlights on the summit road: the ban is printed on every ticket, and rangers swap loaner red bulbs for offenders' lights at the gate.

Proscribe sits at the harsh end of forbidding: the thing is outlawed and publicly condemned, often with penalties attached. And mind the trap — prescribe, its near-twin in spelling, points the opposite way: a doctor prescribes what you must take; a code proscribes what you must not touch.

How Proscribe Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

outlaw

outlaw: puts a thing outside the law's protection

ban

ban: the blunt, everyday word for an official no

Antonyms

permit

permit: officially lets a practice happen

legalize

legalize: brings a once-banned practice inside the law

How Strong Is It? — restrict → prohibit → proscribe

restrict vs. proscribe

restrict vs. proscribe: Restrict is the mildest step — the practice continues, just inside tighter bounds.

prohibit vs. proscribe

prohibit vs. proscribe: Prohibit stops just short of proscribe: both put a thing off limits, but proscribe adds public condemnation — the practice is not merely barred but denounced as a wrong.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pro-

Prefix — pro-: before, in front of, in public

Root — scribe

Root — scribe: to write (Latin scribere)

Put it together

Put it together: Pro- (in front of, in public) + scribe (to write, Latin scribere) = to write up in public. In Rome, being proscribed meant your name was posted on a list of the condemned; the word still carries that public condemnation. Compare circumscribe, on another card of this unit, where the same root draws a boundary instead.

Use the root in a new word: transcribe

Use the root in a new word: transcribe: A volunteer transcribes each oral-history tape, word for word, into the archive.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Proscribe is forbidding at full strength: outlawed, condemned, penalized. Prohibit bans without the thunder; frown on merely disapproves. And spelling is load-bearing here — prescribe, its look-alike, means to order that something BE done. Doctors prescribe; codes proscribe.
